learnPath.title: Learn This Path
learnPath.intro: Grows a reference line beneath your current position (best move at every step, never carded) with deviations branching off it (2nd..Kth choice, recursively explored) to the given depth. A position with no recorded analysis yet is analyzed on demand as the walk reaches it — requires an engine connection. Anchors to an existing card at this position, or marks the current position for minting. Explore first to inspect the grown tree; nothing is minted here — every marked position is added to the batch-mint selection, so review the tree and click Mint Card(s) when ready.

analysis.persist.tooltip:
Experimental — opt-in feature, in active testing.

Save captures whatever the analysis ledger holds for this board right now. Ownership maps and policy heads are only included if the matching overlay was enabled BEFORE the engine ran the analysis — disabling an overlay later does not retroactively add its data to a saved bundle.

Re-saving overwrites the previous bundle entirely; there is no per-record merge.

Closing a board deletes its saved bundle from the server. Bundles auto-restore when the board reappears (e.g., on next SPA load).

Auto-save (engine.katago.analysisAutoSave in the registry, opt-in, default off): when on, the SPA debounces a save call after every authoritative analysis packet so you don't have to click Save manually. The Save button stays available as 'Save now' for an immediate flush outside the throttle window. Auto-save itself is also experimental — quota/too-large failures pause it for the affected board until manual recovery.
analysis.adaptive.tooltip: Adaptive re-evaluation: after the original analysis completes, the proxy re-runs the worst-quantile turns at extra visits and streams the deeper results back as updates. Useful on long range queries where the engine's first pass surfaces moves worth a closer look. Off by default — adaptive's deeper pass changes the visit count of resulting packets, which surprises consumers expecting a specific maxVisits (review-session grading, for example, relies on the card's recorded visit count).
analysis.adaptive.hint: Worst quantile: fraction of moves to re-evaluate (0.05 = top 5% of worst moves; proxy default is 0.25). Extra visits: added to original maxVisits for the deeper pass (proxy default is 800; increment-not-absolute, so the NN cache continues from where the original left off).
analysis.adaptive.valueBinding.label: Value function
analysis.adaptive.valueBinding.experimen: Phase 3.5 LightGBM-supervised predictor. Optimized for modern game positions (~2000+); historical professional records (Shusaku, Dosaku, Go Seigen, Huang Longshi, Fan Xiping, etc.) may benefit from the default built-in allocation instead. Expect ~0.85-0.90 efficiency on modern games vs ~0.46 for the built-in baseline.

qeubo.phaseTooltip: PBO calibrates palette parameters by Bayesian preference learning: it proposes a pair (A vs B), you register your preference, and a Gaussian process refines its model. The Applied/A/B toggle previews each variant; "Use this" promotes the current preview to the persistent parameters; "Pin" saves it as a named bookmark. GP fitting cost is cubic in the number of observations, so each iteration is slower than the last — stop voting once successive bests stabilise (no hard cap is enforced).

wizard.engineUri.details.docker: If you run the Docker bundle, KataGo is configured separately via ENGINE_WS_URL at compose time — this field just points at the bundled proxy.
wizard.engineUri.details.desktop: If you use the desktop app, the bundled proxy's own upstream engine is configured in Settings — this field points at the proxy itself.

wizard.step.palette.title: Default palette
wizard.step.palette.description: This decides how the app judges your moves. Pick whichever style matches how you like to think about mistakes — you can always open Advanced for full control, and switch anytime.
wizard.palette.basic.traditional.label: traditional/severe (I prefer score based view)
wizard.palette.basic.fuzzy.label: fuzzy/lenient (I prefer statistically informed accuracy measurements)
wizard.palette.aggregation.label: Summary over interval:
wizard.palette.describe.score.name: Score Loss
wizard.palette.describe.score.body: Measures how much your move swung the whole-board evaluation — comparing the position immediately before your move to the position immediately after it — as a score-point cost (or gain), correctly credited to whichever color moved. Unlike a 'top move' comparison, this scores every move you actually play, even ones the engine's search never considered listing as a candidate.
wizard.palette.describe.quality.name: Quality (Robust-Child Calibrated)
wizard.palette.describe.quality.body: Measures how closely your move matches the search's most-visited ('robust-child') move, calibrated by how decisively the search favored that move — deviations are judged more leniently in positions where many moves looked reasonable.
wizard.palette.describe.rank.name: Engine Rank
wizard.palette.describe.rank.body: Rewards you by how highly KataGo ranked your move among its candidates — full credit for the top move, half credit for the second choice, and so on — regardless of how far behind it actually scored.
wizard.palette.describe.default.name: Standard Evaluation
wizard.palette.describe.default.body: Uses the same robust-child alignment measure as Quality, but aggregates each interval by its single worst move rather than a median — a stricter reading kept for compatibility with existing profiles.
wizard.palette.editorPointer: For free-form editing, see the Analysis Environment tab in Settings.
wizard.step.demoBoard.title: Try the analysis overlays & PV playback
wizard.step.demoBoard.description: This is an open middle-game position with a pre-computed analysis — no engine connection needed. Toggle the overlays and sliders below and watch the board update, then pick a principal-variation style below and hover a move suggestion on the board to see it play out live.
wizard.demoBoard.loadError: The demo board could not be loaded: {message}
wizard.demoBoard.provenance: Self-play by {model}, move {turn} — analysed at {visits} visits
wizard.pvAnimation.description: When you hover a move suggestion above, its follow-up sequence (principal variation) can be revealed a few different ways. Pick a mode below to try it — the preview underneath replays it immediately, and the same setting applies to every PV shown anywhere in the app.
wizard.pvAnimation.mode.instant.settings: All PV stones fade in together.
wizard.pvAnimation.mode.sequential.setti: Stones fade in one by one (stepDelayMs between each).
wizard.pvAnimation.mode.window.settings: Each stone fades in, holds (windowDurationMs), then fades out.
wizard.pvAnimation.noPreview: No preview available for this demo position.
wizard.step.sgfImport.title: Import your games (optional)
wizard.step.sgfImport.description: If you have SGF files on this device, you can import them into your library now — or skip this and do it later from the Library tab.
wizard.sgfImport.dropHint: Drag an SGF file or a folder of SGFs here, or:
wizard.sgfImport.staged: no files staged | one file staged — it will be imported when you finish the wizard | {count} files staged — they will be imported when you finish the wizard
wizard.sgfImport.result.errored: Import finished with {count} of {total} file(s) failed — check the Library tab for details.
wizard.step.finish.title: You're all set
wizard.step.finish.description: Here's your current setup — steps you didn't visit are still on their defaults. Everything is saved and also visible in Settings.
wizard.finish.sgfImport.staged: no files staged | one file staged for import | {count} files staged for import
wizard.finish.hint: You can re-run this wizard anytime from Settings → Session (UI).
